headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Plandex can write/modify the shared project sandbox while RisingWave is a data system with no documented isolation, but prompt-injection and leakage are not evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex ingests files and can execute shell commands, but RisingWave has no documented output channel into Plandex and no shared MCP/clipboard bridge is shown. The only plausible pathway is manual or workspace-mediated content transfer, so injection risk is limited and not default. Uncertainty is low because both profiles lack a direct bridging surface.
conditions: IF RisingWave output is copied into Plandex prompts or files, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace, file-based instruction smuggling becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep RisingWave outputs out of Plandex prompt inputs.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex.
Review any imported text before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex can read and write a project directory and has broad network egress, while RisingWave shows no data classes touched and no egress. The pair does not document a shared workspace or sensitive data class, so leakage is possible only if the operator co-locates files. Because the interaction is undocumented, uncertainty stays on the lower side but not none.
conditions: IF both agents share the same filesystem path, Plandex may read data intended for RisingWave.
IF sensitive source code is placed in Plandex's project directory, it can be sent to external model providers.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces.
Restrict Plandex to non-sensitive repos.
Disable broad egress where possible.
Rotate or remove API keys from shared directories.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; RisingWave is a data-engineering system with no concurrency or locking details. If both touch the same repo or mutable resource, write conflicts are plausible in default multi-instance use via Plandex's shared backend. Because RisingWave's write surfaces are undocumented, uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout, concurrent writes can conflict.
IF RisingWave is configured to mutate shared mutable resources, Plandex may overwrite or race those changes.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or clones.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
Review git diffs before apply.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex uses a review-then-apply workflow, but it can still generate plans that another system may treat as authoritative. RisingWave has no documented verification layer or downstream action policy, so if its outputs are fed into Plandex or vice versa, errors can cascade across work products. The pathway exists by composition, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF RisingWave outputs are used as inputs to Plandex plans, unverified facts can propagate.
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled, a mistaken plan can become a committed change.
mitigations: Require human review of all generated plans.
Disable auto-apply.
Cross-check outputs against source data.
Limit one agent to drafting only.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Plandex explicitly handles model provider API keys and broad network egress, while RisingWave documents no data residency or retention constraints. No PHI, EU PII, or regulated data class is evidenced, so this is a compliance-gap risk only if the operator routes regulated data through Plandex. The other agent is not cited because its profile lacks a relevant compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Plandex prompts or files, external model-provider transfer may create compliance obligations.
IF the deployment requires residency controls, Plandex's broad egress may violate them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of prompts.
Use a self-hosted model path if available.
Review retention settings.
Document data flows.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
